verdict.rationale: MotherDuck documents its own role-based sharing: read access can be granted to users or preset roles, and an include pattern limits which tables and views a Share exposes. That gives table-level isolation that teams and tenants can use. There is no evidence of column-level grants, row-level security, or masking policies, which are the core of the story's fine-grained requirement. Missing for 10: column-level access control, row-level security policies, data masking policies, custom role definitions beyond preset roles, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, access control reaches tables, columns, and rows — roles plus masking policies — so one warehouse can serve many teams safely

citations.quote: Grant read access to users or roles for multi-tenant applications and collaboration.
Limit which tables and views a Share exposes with an include pattern.
Sharing data with specific preset roles or accounts in your organization. This is popular with data application builders that need to isolate tenants.
